speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your infant is experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. Can you tell me exactly what activities or positions seem to trigger these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Those triggers—crying, feeding, and neck flexion—are highly suggestive of a vascular ring or similar structural anomaly compressing the airway and esophagus. Has the child experienced any difficulty swallowing solids or liquids, or signs of respiratory distress at rest?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of stridor, wheezing, and vomiting that worsens with neck flexion and feeding strongly points to a vascular ring, such as a double aortic arch. I will order imaging to confirm this structural anomaly. REQUEST TEST: CT_Angiography_Chest

speaker: Doctor
text: That is unexpected, as a normal CT angiography typically rules out vascular rings like a double aortic arch. Let me request the images to verify the findings and ensure no subtle anomalies were missed. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Born full term with no complications during birth. Social history: First child in the family. Lives with both parents. No exposure to smoking or pets in the household.
